Table 3. ADULT BURN RESUSCITATION FORMULAS (หัวตาราง: Formula · First 24 Hours [Crystalloid · Colloid · Glucose in Water] · Second 24 Hours [Crystalloid · Colloid · Glucose in Water])
Evans: First 24 h — Crystalloid: Normal saline 1 mL/kg/% burn · Colloid: 1 mL/kg/% burn · Glucose in Water: 2000 mL · Second 24 h — Crystalloid: 50% of first 24-h requirement · Colloid: 50% of first 24-h requirement · Glucose in Water: 2000 mL
Brooke: First 24 h — Crystalloid: Lactated Ringer's 1.5 mL/kg/% burn · Colloid: 0.5 mL/kg/% burn · Glucose in Water: 2000 mL · Second 24 h — Crystalloid: 50%–75% of first 24-h requirement · Colloid: 50%–75% of first 24 hour rquirement · Glucose in Water: 2000 mL
Parkland: First 24 h — Crystalloid: Lactated Ringer's 4 mL/kg/% burn · Colloid: — · Glucose in Water: — · Second 24 h — Crystalloid: — · Colloid: 20%–60% of calculated plasma volume · Glucose in Water: Titrated to maintain urinary output
Modified Brooke: First 24 h — Crystalloid: Lactated Ringer's 2 mL/kg/% burn · Colloid: — · Glucose in Water: — · Second 24 h — Crystalloid: — · Colloid: 0.3–0.5 mL/kg/% burn · Glucose in Water: Titrated to maintain urinary output
Hypertonic saline (Monafo): First 24 h — Crystalloid: Titrate solution containing 250 mEq Na/liter to maintain urinary output · Colloid: — · Glucose in Water: — · Second 24 h — Crystalloid: Titrate to maintain urinary output with ⅓ normal saline · Colloid: — · Glucose in Water: —
Modified hypertonic (MetroHealth Medical Center): First 24 h — Crystalloid: Lactated Ringer's plus 50 mEq NaHCO3 (180 mEq Na/liter) Lactated Ringer's 4 mL/kg/% burn titrated to urine output for remainder of 24 hours · Colloid: — · Glucose in Water: — · Second 24 h — Crystalloid: Titrate to maintain urinary output with ½ normal saline · Colloid: One unit FFP for each liter of ½ normal saline · Glucose in Water: As needed to prevent hypo-glycemia

Thermal injury suggested fluid resuscitation (modified Parkland formula)Day 1: (Hour 0 = time burn occurred) (hour 0-24)
Lactated Ringer’s Solution
Total volume for 24 hr = 4cc/Kg/%burn · Give 1/2 of total volume in 1st 8hr · Give 1/2 of total volume in 2nd 16hr
Adjust infusion rate as necessary to keep urine output: · Adults: 30-50 cc/hr · Children: 1.0 cc/Kg/Hr

Day 2: Hours 25-48
Change lactated Ringer’s to D5W and adjust based on urine output as above.
Begin colloid infusion: 5% Albumin at 0.3-1.0 cc/Kg/% burn/16 =cc 5% albumin/hr. Do not vary based on urine output.
Day 3: (hours 49+)
Change to maintenance IV or begin po intake and/or enteral feedings.
For patients with burns >40% to 50% or in the presence of significant inhalation injury or previously existing cardiorespiratory disease, consider beginning colloid earlier (hour 8-24) and continuing through day 2.
